parts.name: Payout set-up
parts.what: Creator payout set-up on the kit's payouts (KIT-A3-F3-P1), including the identity checks the provider needs (KIT-A2-F1-P2).

parts.name: Earnings and statements
parts.what: Balance, payouts and statements on the kit's earnings page (KIT-A3-F3-P3).

features.name: Tax done right
features.does: Get the tax summaries you need, with GST handled where the platform must collect it.

parts.name: Tax research for creator payments
parts.what: Which of the kit's tax rules apply to creator payments: GST on digital services, who is the seller of record (KIT-A3-F1-P5), income reporting to IRD and overseas tax; needs a tax adviser's view.

parts.name: Tax summaries
parts.what: Yearly and on-demand summaries for creators from the kit's statements and IRD reporting (KIT-A4-F4-P1, KIT-A4-F3-P3).

parts.name: GST as the deemed supplier
parts.what: Where NZ GST law treats the co-op as the supplier of remote services sold through Spare Social, such as memberships and paid videos from offshore creators to NZ consumers (GST Act section 60C), works out, collects, invoices and returns the GST; until overseas tax is handled (SOC-A15-F13), paid content is sold only to NZ buyers. Needs a tax adviser's view.

features.name: Honest sponsorship labels
features.does: Mark a post as a paid partnership and tag the brand, so viewers always know.

parts.name: Paid partnership label
parts.what: A label and brand tag on posts, searchable and shown in every feed.

parts.name: Advertising rules research
parts.what: NZ Advertising Standards rules for influencers and overseas equivalents.

parts.name: Promotion the law bans
parts.what: Sponsored posts for things NZ law bans promoting, such as vaping and tobacco products, offshore gambling and some medicines, are not allowed even with a label, and election posts carry the promoter statement the Electoral Act asks for.

features.name: Link your shop
features.does: Tag products from your Spare Market shop or your own site in posts and on your profile.

parts.name: Product tags
parts.what: Product tags that open the Spare Market listing, drawn from the kit's listing model (KIT-A5-F1-P1); checkout stays in Spare Market.

features.name: Refunds and payment disputes
features.does: Ask for a refund on a membership or purchase and have disputes handled fairly.

parts.name: Refunds and chargebacks
parts.what: Refunds, card disputes and who carries a loss on the kit's refunds, disputes and loss rules (KIT-A3-F5-P1, KIT-A3-F5-P2, KIT-A3-F16-P1), with member-panel disputes on the shared trust service.

features.name: No adverts, ever
features.does: Use Spare Social with no adverts and no data sold, now and later.

parts.name: No-advert rule
parts.what: A co-op rule that bans adverts and data sales, changeable only under the protected-rules process (SOC-A22-F1-P3); an advert is a placement the platform sells, so creators' own labelled sponsorships (SOC-A15-F6) are not adverts.

features.name: Pay on any device
features.does: Pay for memberships, paid videos, tips and storage in a way each app store allows, so creators keep everything except payment fees on iPhone and Android too.

parts.name: App store payment rules
parts.what: When Apple and Google require their own in-app purchase, with a 15 to 30 percent cut, for memberships, paid videos, tips and storage fees; which exemptions apply, such as Apple's rule on optional gifts that pass in full to the receiver (guideline 3.2.1, current text to be checked); and where linking out is allowed, such as the US since May 2025.

parts.name: Purchase plan per country
parts.what: For each storefront, buy on the web only, link out where allowed, or use reader-app style access, so a store's cut is never hidden in a creator's price.

features.name: Safe from payment fraud and laundering
features.does: Know tips and memberships are protected from stolen cards, card testing and money laundering.

parts.name: Tip and membership fraud checks
parts.what: Card testing, stolen-card tips and self-tipping caught with the kit's fraud screening and published risk rules (KIT-A3-F13-P1, KIT-A3-F13-P2).

parts.name: Payout holds and negative balances
parts.what: New creators' first payouts are held for a published time, and negative balances after chargebacks are recovered within the kit's limits (KIT-A3-F16-P2).

parts.name: Anti-money-laundering and sanctions
parts.what: Whether DIA's anti-money-laundering rules for online marketplaces cover creator tips and memberships (unverified), under the kit's programme (KIT-A4-F5-P1), and sanctions screening of payouts through the provider (KIT-A4-F8-P1).

features.name: Share earnings and give memberships
features.does: Split earnings with co-authors, channel teams and series collaborators, and give someone a membership as a gift.

parts.name: Revenue splits
parts.what: Agreed shares of tips, memberships and sales for co-authored posts, channel teams and series collaborators, each paid out separately.

parts.name: Gift memberships
parts.what: Buy a membership for someone else, who can accept or decline it.

features.name: Sell to buyers overseas
features.does: Sell memberships and paid videos to buyers in other countries with their VAT or GST handled.

parts.name: Overseas VAT on digital sales
parts.what: Works out, collects and returns VAT or GST where EU, UK, Australian and other platform rules make the co-op responsible for electronic services, using the kit's tax rules per country (KIT-A4-F7-P1); needs a tax adviser's view.

areas.name: Creator studio and stats
areas.summary: One place for creators to see how their work is doing without tracking anyone, manage everything they have posted, handle comments and messages, work as a team, deal with copyright claims, and publish straight from Spare Studio.

features.name: See how your work is doing
features.does: See views, watch time, how long people stay, and followers gained, for each post and over time.

parts.name: Private counting
parts.what: Views and watch time counted in aggregate on the kit's private usage counts (KIT-A22-F8-P1), with no per-person tracking kept.

parts.name: Stats dashboard
parts.what: Per-post and per-channel views, watch time, retention curve and followers gained.

parts.name: Safe audience summaries
parts.what: Audience summaries such as country or language only for groups large enough that no one can be singled out.

parts.name: Export your stats
parts.what: Download stats as CSV or JSON.

features.name: Manage all your content
features.does: Search, filter and bulk-edit your posts and videos: visibility, captions, playlists and licence.

parts.name: Content manager
parts.what: A table of everything you posted with filters and bulk actions, each an operation you can undo, with a link to fix a published video (SOC-A6-F10).

features.name: One inbox for comments and messages
features.does: Read and answer comments, mentions and messages from one place, with filters.

parts.name: Creator inbox
parts.what: Comments, mentions and messages together, with filters for unanswered, members and keywords.

features.name: Work as a team
features.does: Give editors, managers and moderators access to your channel without sharing your login.

parts.name: Channel team roles
parts.what: Team roles with a log of who did what.

features.name: Handle copyright claims
features.does: See claims against your videos, answer them, and track the outcome.

parts.name: Claims centre
parts.what: Your copyright notices, counter-notices and appeals in one place.

features.name: Publish from Spare Studio
features.does: Send a finished video or photo from Spare Studio straight to your channel.

parts.name: Publish through the command API
parts.what: Spare Studio publishes using Spare Social's public command API, not shared code; the post goes to the section its AI-use answer gives (SOC-A11-F3-P2), never to the AI section just because software posted it.

parts.name: Bulk upload
parts.what: Upload many videos at once with details, including each one's AI-use answer, from a spreadsheet.

areas.name: Media pipeline and delivery
areas.summary: The machinery under every photo and video: uploads that survive bad connections, transcoding into sizes for streaming, codec choices that avoid patent costs, image processing, storage and delivery at cost, automatic captions, safe handling of harmful files and links, fair use of storage, and deletion that really deletes.

features.name: Upload anything reliably
features.does: Upload photos and long videos that pause and resume on a bad connection, with hidden location data removed.

parts.name: Resumable uploads
parts.what: Chunked uploads that resume after a drop, on the kit's one file service (KIT-A15-F7-P1) using the open tus protocol, with limits sized for long videos.

parts.name: Upload checks
parts.what: File type, size and quota checks from the kit's file service (KIT-A15-F7-P1), plus Spare Social's checks on video and audio files inside the sandbox (SOC-A17-F7-P1).

parts.name: Strip hidden data
parts.what: Uses the kit's photo metadata stripping (KIT-A15-F7-P3) and does the same for videos: GPS location and device details removed by default.

parts.name: Original kept
parts.what: Keep the original file for export and for transcoding again later.

features.name: Videos play smoothly anywhere
features.does: Watch any video that starts fast and adjusts to your connection, from slow rural mobile to fibre.

parts.name: Transcoding ladder
parts.what: Turn each upload into several sizes and bitrates for streaming.

parts.name: Codec choice and patents
parts.what: Compare AV1, VP9, H.264 and HEVC on quality, device support, cost and patent licensing.

parts.name: Streaming packaging
parts.what: Package videos for adaptive streaming with HLS and DASH.

parts.name: Thumbnails and preview strips
parts.what: Make thumbnails and scrub-bar previews for every video.

parts.name: Even loudness
parts.what: Level audio so videos play at a steady volume.

parts.name: Transcoding job queue
parts.what: Queue and workers for transcoding, recording machine time per video for the cost ledger.

features.name: Photos look right and load fast
features.does: See sharp photos in the right colours that load quickly, even on slow connections.

parts.name: Image sizes and formats
parts.what: Photo sizes from the kit's file service (KIT-A15-F7-P1), served as AVIF and WebP with JPEG as a fallback.

parts.name: Colour and HDR photos
parts.what: Keep colour profiles and HDR photos correct from camera to screen.

parts.name: Blur-up placeholders
parts.what: Tiny previews that show while the full photo loads.

features.name: Delivered at cost
features.does: Get videos and photos from storage and delivery that cost as little as possible, with the costs published.

parts.name: Storage with tiers
parts.what: Object storage with hot and cold tiers, moving old, rarely watched files to cheaper storage.

parts.name: Delivery network choice
parts.what: Compare co-op caches, delivery networks bought at cost and member servers on cost and reach in NZ and overseas.

parts.name: Peer-assisted playback
parts.what: Viewers share pieces of videos with each other to cut bandwidth, written as our own code.

parts.name: Signed media links
parts.what: Time-limited links from the kit's file service and sharing rules (KIT-A15-F7-P1, KIT-A15-F8-P1), so private and members-only media cannot be passed around.

parts.name: Metering for the ledger
parts.what: Measure storage and bandwidth per program, per creator and per member for the open cost ledger.

features.name: Automatic captions
features.does: Get captions made for every video and voice note, then fix them if needed.

parts.name: Speech to text
parts.what: Speech recognition through the kit's captions (KIT-A19-F4-P1): an openly licensed model run at cost, te reo Māori and English first.

parts.name: Caption files
parts.what: WebVTT and SRT caption files with correct timing, from the kit's captions library (KIT-A19-F4-P1).

parts.name: Spoken language detection
parts.what: Detect the language spoken so captions use the right model.

features.name: Deleted means deleted
features.does: When you delete a photo or video, every copy, size and cached piece on Spare Social's servers is gone within a published time, and other servers are asked to delete theirs.

parts.name: Deletion fan-out
parts.what: Removes every size, copy, delivery cache and peer piece, on top of the kit's deletion (KIT-A18-F2-P1), and confirms when done.

parts.name: Legal hold
parts.what: Keep evidence only when the law requires it, such as reported child abuse material, sealed and logged.

parts.name: Deletes sent across the network
parts.what: Sends delete requests to every server a post reached, and says plainly in the privacy statement that servers on the open network may keep copies.

features.name: Media handled safely
features.does: Know a booby-trapped file or link cannot break into Spare Social's servers.

parts.name: Sandboxed media processing
parts.what: Transcoders and media parsers run in a locked-down sandbox with no network access, so a harmful video file cannot take over a server.

parts.name: Safe outside fetches
parts.what: Link previews, the remote content cache and feed imports refuse internal and private addresses, follow few redirects and cap size and time, so no one can use them to reach our own systems (server-side request forgery).

features.name: Fair use of storage

parts.name: ActivityPub server

parts.name: AT Protocol server

features.name: Take your followers with you

parts.what: Moving accounts and followers with each protocol's own move method.

parts.name: Member-held keys

features.name: Run your own Spare Social server

parts.name: Server-to-server moderation

features.name: See outside posts safely

features.name: Learn from existing open networks

parts.name: Protocol library licence check

features.name: Take your posts with you

areas.name: Your data and privacy

features.name: Privacy settings

features.name: No tracking and no adverts

assess: Would the core features alone make a credible switch for someone leaving TikTok, YouTube, Instagram or Facebook, and which one should the first release aim at?
Is a time-order feed plus a discovery feed with published rules enough to keep people who are used to TikTok's For You feed?
Can the co-op afford video storage and bandwidth at cost (piece M06), and would members accept a free allowance with at-cost storage for heavy uploaders?
Which open protocol comes first (piece M01), which Spare Social promises can it not carry (SOC-A18-F1-P6), and is moving your followers really part of the first release?

Is the line between personal filters and legal removal clear, and does 'remove only what the law requires' hold up against NZ duties, overseas laws and other governments' demands (pieces M02, SOC-A13-F3-P7)?
Can elected volunteer moderators meet 24 and 48-hour legal deadlines around the clock, or does the co-op need paid, vetted staff on call (SOC-A13-F3-P8, SOC-A13-F7)?
Should lawful adult sexual content be allowed with full age and consent checks, kept out of the app-store apps, or ruled out (SOC-A13-F2-P4)?
How does Spare Social meet minimum-age laws, such as Australia's under-16 law and NZ's August 2026 bill, without keeping identity documents?
Is short video workable without commercial music, and what would licensing music in NZ cost at cost?
Is end-to-end encrypted messaging right for the first release, and is reporting from the reporter's own device enough for safety?
